real_vulnerability_hit_analysis.task: Determine whether the real vulnerabilities (user-provided PyVul-style commit records) were hit by the Pass 5 formal analysis.
real_vulnerability_hit_analysis.overall_verdict: 0 of 4 real vulnerability commits were hit. The Pass 5 formal query returned zero results, and for each candidate the analyzed snapshot either already contains the security fix, contains only parameter-bound flows, or does not contain the vulnerable code at all.

function_presence_in_snapshot.matches_code_before: Yes — the snapshot contains the exact code_before: 'def _convert_field_to_tz(self, sql, params, tzname)' with body 'return f"CONVERT_TZ({sql}, %s, %s)", (*params, self.connection.timezone_name, self._prepare_tzname_delta(tzname))'. The 5e2f4ddf rename to _convert_sql_to_tz has NOT been applied in this 4.2.0-alpha0 snapshot.

analysis: This commit is a naming refactor ('Refs CVE-2022-34265 -- Unified ... hook names'), not the security fix itself. The actual CVE-2022-34265 fix (regex whitelist validating lookup_type before its f-string interpolation into EXTRACT(...)) IS present in the analyzed snapshot: mysql/operations.py:42 defines '_extract_format_re = _lazy_re_compile(r"[A-Z_]+")' and mysql/operations.py:63-66 does 'lookup_type = lookup_type.upper(); if not self._extract_format_re.fullmatch(lookup_type): raise ValueError(...)' before 'return f"EXTRACT({lookup_type} FROM {sql})"'. The exploitable pre-fix pattern does not exist in the analyzed DB.

Within _convert_field_to_tz itself, the only externally influenced value, tzname, is passed as a BOUND parameter: the template 'CONVERT_TZ({sql}, %s, %s)' places {sql} (the ORM-compiled column expression, not attacker text) in the SQL string and pushes tzname/timezone_name into the params tuple. No taint reaches the SQL text channel here; the bound-parameter channel is by design not a SQL-text sink.

The CVE is a framework-gadget vulnerability: exploitation requires APPLICATION code to pass untrusted data as kind/lookup_name to Trunc()/Extract(). The analyzed DB contains only the Django framework and its own tests; no HTTP-request-boundary source (request.GET/POST/... , environ, URL kwargs) flows into Extract(lookup_name=...) or Trunc(kind=...) anywhere in the snapshot. Hence the Pass 5 query legitimately finds no path.

Sink reality check: even if a tainted lookup_name existed, the sink chain would be real (Extract.as_sql -> connection.ops.datetime_extract_sql -> date_extract_sql -> f-string EXTRACT text -> compiled SQL -> cursor.execute), but the snapshot's regex whitelist (mysql/operations.py:64) acts as a sanitizer exactly on this fragment, and no source-to-here path exists.
hits.source_evidence: No source: no request-derived value reaches datetime_extract_sql's lookup_type or Trunc's kind in the snapshot (framework + tests only).
hits.sink_evidence: django/db/backends/mysql/operations.py:66 (snapshot) — EXTRACT f-string; guarded by :63-65 validation.
hits.barrier_evidence: mysql/operations.py:42 + :63-65 (_extract_format_re whitelist on lookup_type); mysql/operations.py:94-98 (tzname as bound %s parameter).

function_presence_in_snapshot.matches_code_before: No — the snapshot already contains the code_after shape: 'value = super().get_prep_value(value); if value is None: return None; return str(value)'. The vulnerable code_before (returning the raw value with no type coercion) does not exist in the analyzed 4.2.0-alpha0 snapshot.

analysis: The affected line (Django <= 1.6.2) predates the snapshot by roughly nine major versions; FilePathField.get_prep_value in the snapshot is the fixed, str-coercing version.

The 2013 MySQL typecasting issue is fundamentally a type-coercion / filter-bypass weakness (a non-string-typed value compared against a string column could make MySQL cast the column side), not a taint-flow SQL injection: no attacker-controlled text ever enters SQL syntax. Even on a vulnerable 1.6-era tree, a CWE-89 taint query correctly would not and should not flag get_prep_value, because the value is always delivered as a bound parameter, never interpolated into SQL text.
Pass 5 returned zero formal results, so this is trivially not hit.
hits.source_evidence: N/A — no path exists in the formal results.
hits.sink_evidence: N/A — values from get_prep_value are used as bound parameters, not SQL text.
hits.barrier_evidence: Parameter binding throughout the ORM value channel (compiler.py execute(sql, params) in the snapshot).

function_presence_in_snapshot.matches_code_before: No — same as the 1.6.x entry: the snapshot contains the post-fix code_after.

analysis: Backport commit for the same 2013 issue; identical reasoning to the 1.6.x entry above. The vulnerable code is absent from the analyzed snapshot, the issue is not a taint-flow SQL injection, and the formal Pass 5 result set is empty.

Note: the code_before snippet in the user-provided record (GenericIPAddressField-style body with clean_ipv6_address) still exists in the snapshot at django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:2148-2155, but the surrounding Field/CharField get_prep_value chain now coerces values to text, which is exactly what the 2013 fix added; the snippet alone does not reproduce the vulnerability.

function_presence_in_snapshot.matches_code_before: No — smart_unicode/six-era code is long gone; the snapshot is 4.2.0-alpha0 with the modern fixed implementation.

analysis: Backport commit for the same 2013 issue; identical reasoning. Vulnerable code absent from the analyzed snapshot, the issue is a type-conversion weakness rather than a taint-flow SQL injection, and Pass 5 formal results are empty.

real_vulnerability_hit_analysis.summary: Pass 5 formal results: 0 alerts, so none of the 4 real-vulnerability commits were hit. For CVE-2022-34265 the analyzed 4.2.0-alpha0 snapshot already contains the security fix (_extract_format_re whitelist at mysql/operations.py:42/63-66), the cited _convert_field_to_tz code_before exists but passes tzname only as a bound parameter, and no request-boundary source reaches kind/lookup_name in the framework-only code base. For the three 2013 MySQL typecasting commits, the vulnerable code is absent from the snapshot (fixed long before 4.2.0-alpha0) and the issue is not a taint-flow SQL injection in the first place. Detecting CVE-2022-34265's gadget with a request-source taint query would require either a pre-fix (pre-3.2.14/4.0.6) snapshot or application-level code passing request data into Trunc()/Extract(), neither of which is present.
